context.user-input: the first Glyph session in the cloud: build the series layout, then run the EMS-001 queue from ORD-0001 for as long as the budget lasts
a clone of github.com/Trevojan/glyph on a Linux machine, at the commit that carries this handoff
engine 3.5.8.06, the work of 2026-09-24 committed, ORD-0011 parked, everything the EMS-001 spec revokes signed

instruction.user-input: hear this order, ground before building, bank every step before the next, and stop at the gates of the Regent

define-symbol.user-input: who decides; this session measures, proposes and refuses, and never ratifies a norm it wrote
the spec of EMS-001: .guidelines/.orders/ORD-0012.pgml until the layout moves it to .guidelines/.orders/EMS-001/EMS-001.pgml
a commit that passes npm run check and npm run check:rust, pushed to the session branch, with the return updated in the same commit
.guidelines/.orders/EMS-001/RETURN.md, the file the Regent reads first when the session ends, however it ends
its val holds, its work is banked, and its row is written in the track of the spec, in EMS-001/README.md and in the where-am-I table of .shortcuts

note.user-input: the budget is finite and can end in the middle of a step; what is not banked is lost, so a small banked step is worth more than a large unbanked one
this session is also a measurement of the cloud: what it closes, how long each step takes and where it stalls is part of what it delivers

requirement.user-input: node 18 or later, and cargo; run node --version and cargo --version before anything else

instruction.user-input: if cargo is missing, install it with rustup; if it cannot be installed, do the layout, bank it, write the return and stop

note.user-input: the Rust workspace holds no crate from outside the repository, so cargo builds offline
.gitattributes forces LF everywhere, and the oracle is written at the commit under test, so it is never compared across machines
the slash commands under commands/ need the plugin installed; here, call node scripts/glyph-plugin.js and node scripts/glyph-cli.js directly
this machine is Linux: ORD-0013, the installer, and ORD-0014, the window, are for Windows and never run here

constraint.user-input: work on the branch this session was given, and push to it after every bank

where.user-input: CLAUDE.md, then .guidelines/.shortcuts/README.md, then .constraints, .decisions and .plan, in that order

requirement.user-input: npm run check and npm run check:rust pass on the clone before anything is touched

finally.user-input: the session here if either fails on the clone, with the failure and its output in the return

note.user-input: the references of the skill are long: open the section a question needs, not the whole file

target.user-input: the series layout: .guidelines/.orders/EMS-###/ holds the spec of its series and one folder ORD-####/ per order, and the count of ORD restarts in each series

instruction.user-input: git mv the spec to .guidelines/.orders/EMS-001/EMS-001.pgml, and rewrite every pointer to it in the same commit: .plan, .shortcuts, .decisions, the briefing and this handoff

teach --bundle in scripts/glyph-cli.js the series: when --out is a folder named EMS-###, the ORD is written as a folder ORD-####/ holding the five files the zip holds today, numbered by the ORD folders of that series alone
the number reads an ID only when ORD-#### is followed by nothing, a dot or the end of a folder name, so ORD-2026-08-30-01 stops counting as 2026 in every destination
teach scripts/glyph-plugin.js the series: --from takes EMS-001/ORD-0003 as well as a path or a bare ORD-####
teach commands/repo-config/guidelines/orders/bundle.md the series: its probes list the series and read the open ORD from EMS-###/README.md
write .guidelines/.orders/EMS-001/README.md with the two sections the bundle command reads, A Ordem aberta and Ordens fechadas

note.user-input: the Regent delegates to this session the open and closed lines of EMS-001 alone

mandatory.user-input: every new behaviour gets a check in the bundle bucket of scripts/test-corpus.js, observed failing before the code that makes it pass
run node scripts/build-templates.js and node scripts/build-skill.js after touching the engine, and let their --check decide

constraint.user-input: the emitir ORD button of the app stays as it is: the browser sees no folder, and its number stays in localStorage

note.user-input: whether an ORD of a series also travels as a .zip is the Regent’s question; write the folder, and put the question in the return

validate.user-input: the bundle emits EMS-001/ORD-0001/ on its first call and ORD-0002 on its second, a dated ID beside them changes nothing, and npm run check passes

instruction.user-input: run the ORDs of the spec in the order of their numbers, one open at a time, each one through the same five steps

author: write the source of the ORD from its section of the spec alone, under a block whose ctx names the spec; add nothing the section does not say, and leave a gap as an empty slot so it travels as needs
emit: node scripts/glyph-plugin.js --from the source --bundle --out .guidelines/.orders/EMS-001, then mark it open in EMS-001/README.md, and bank
work: one step per commit, each one banked
prove: run the val of the ORD as the spec writes it, and keep the output that proves it
close: write its row in the track of the spec, in EMS-001/README.md and in .shortcuts, with the commit and the digest it matched, and bank

constraint.user-input: one ORD open at a time: the asynchronous pairs in the queue section of the spec are a proposal the Regent has not signed

mandatory.user-input: the oracle is the test: node scripts/test-corpus.js --export-oracle writes it to rust/target/oracle at the commit under test
a Rust test that finds no oracle fails and names the command that writes it; it never passes empty

never.user-input: fix a JS defect inside an ORD: the oracle is what the JS answers, defects included; the Rust answers the same bytes, and the defect goes to the return

note.user-input: ORD-0001 closes with the tag conformance-v0 on its commit, pushed with it
the spans of ORD-0004 are counted in UTF-16 code units, as the JS counts them

finally.user-input: the queue at the first ORD whose val needs the Regent: ORD-0010 ends in an ADR the Regent signs, so it is measured, the ADR is written as a proposal in the return, and it stays open
the queue when a crate from outside the repository would enter: measure its tree by the filter of INTAKE-RUST-LADDER section 9, put the measurement in the return, and let it wait
the queue when the Rust would need a feature the JS lacks, or the snapshot would need regenerating
the queue when the budget is near its end: bank what is green, write the return, and push

instruction.user-input: keep the return current in every bank commit, so it is true whenever the session ends
write in it: where the session is; each ORD closed, with its commit and the digest it matched; what is open and why; what was measured
write the questions for the Regent as closed questions, each with its options, none answered
write what the session measured of itself: the ORDs closed, the commits banked, the time from each ORD opening to its closing as the commits date it, the checks that failed and what fixed them

never.user-input: the snapshot is regenerated to make the suite green
push to main, force a push, or rewrite a banked commit

do-not.user-input: open an ORD before the ORDs it depends on close
let a feature land in Rust that the JS engine lacks; new vocabulary enters the stores and the JS first
touch ORD-0011, the flat ORD files of .orders, or .scope, which is the workspace of the Regent

constraint.user-input: prose declares the state, never the correction
what travels is spelt en-EU, the interface stays pt-BR, and commit messages follow the pt-BR of the log

verify.user-input: npm run check and npm run check:rust pass on the last commit, and it is pushed

ready.user-input: the Regent opens the return and knows, without this conversation, what was built, what it matched, and what waits for the Regent
